subject.title: fix: require decimal numeric oc-path predicates

question: Should relational oc-path predicates continue to accept all finite JavaScript numeric forms, or should OpenClaw intentionally narrow the supported grammar to plain decimal values only?
rationale: The patch changes a previously accepted input grammar into silent false results; tests can verify either choice, but cannot determine which compatibility contract maintainers intend to support.

options.title: Keep finite-number compatibility
options.body: Retain finite-number parsing for relational predicates and limit any fix to malformed or non-finite values without rejecting valid exponent-form numbers.

options.title: Adopt decimal-only predicates
options.body: Approve the narrower grammar explicitly, document it as a compatibility change, and keep focused tests for every accepted and rejected form.

recommendation.title: Keep finite-number compatibility
recommendation.body: Retain finite-number parsing for relational predicates and limit any fix to malformed or non-finite values without rejecting valid exponent-form numbers.

likelyOwner.reason: The timeline shows involvement in the prior review escalation for this predicate-contract decision.
